newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates steady in quiet business.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates steady in quiet business.

text.p: Crude tanker rates were fairly steady on Monday in a quiet market, with the absence of many U.S. brokers from the market due to the President's Day holiday dampening trade.
"It's pretty quiet with the States closed," said one broker. "Also a lot of people are absent from the market due to IP (Institute of Petroleum) week."
Middle East rates were little changed with a Japan-bound VLCC assessed at W65, while VLCCs headed for Singapore and Thailand drifted around the W45-46 range.
"We could see this easing as the week progresses if trade doesn't pick up," said the broker.
The UK-Continental market remained fairly choppy with 130,000 tonners doing cross UK-cont trips reported at W92.5-100.

Brokers said rates for the sector could soften if bad weather in the North Sea persisted. Berthing at Sullom Voe was suspended on Sunday due to high winds which were expected to continue until Tuesday.
While crude loadings at Norway's Stafjord and Gullfaks fields was stopped on Monday due to hurricane force winds.
"If it goes on for more than 24 hours we could see tonnage beginning to bunch up which could hurt rates," another broker said.
The Meditteranean was steady to slightly higher, although brokers said trade remained fairly subdued. Rates for 130,000 tonners were assessed at W90 and 80,000 tonners were put at W120-125.
The West African market was fairly buoyant with 130,000 tonners headed for the US Gulf fixed at W88-90.
"It's fairly busy," said one broker. "Rates are fairly steady but it really depends what kind of tonnage you want."
The Carribean market was quiet due to the U.S. holiday. Rates for 76,000 tonners were reported at W105-106.
